learning: Compare this race with iteration 0. If max_error and steering_oscillation rise together on the slalom, reduce kp toward 2.0 and kd should stay at 0.4. If progress on the s-bend stays near 0.24 with no oscillation, the limit is turn authority: raise kp toward 3.0 or keep base_speed lower on bends.
notes: Builder's proposed geometry with a controller tuned for it: kp held at 2.5 because the narrower track already raises turn rate, kd raised to 0.4 to damp lookahead lag, and base_speed raised to 1.8 for the sub-3 s finish target.
rationale: Iteration 0 is the only race evidence. The baseline (score 184.5) finished 3 of 60 trials, all on the oval. The s-bend (progress 0.24) and slalom (progress 0.11) both ended off-track, with about one line-loss event per run and a steady rms_error near 0.025. That pattern points to insufficient turn authority or late reaction at bends, not sensor noise. The Builder's geometry (wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.035, mass 0.6, sensors at y=0.07 spanning ±0.03 m) is within every contract limit, so I keep it unchanged. Sensor weights stay proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so a centred line gives signal 0 and the signal scale is unchanged despite the narrower array. The narrower track raises turn rate per unit of kp, so I keep kp at 2.5 rather than raising it further, which limits the risk of overshoot. The forward offset adds lookahead lag, so kd rises from 0.3 to 0.4 for damping. base_speed rises from 1.6 to 1.8 to help the sub-3 s finish, accepting some risk of off-track on the tightest bends. ki stays at 0.05 to avoid integral wind-up on one-sided bends. line_loss stays last_direction so the robot recovers toward the side it last saw tape. Expected result: more s-bend progress and fewer off-track ends. The main risk is oscillation from the forward offset and higher speed together.
